To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) we have prepared extracts from calli that contain high protein content; (2) we have separated the proteins in non‐equilibrium gels and identified the proteins whose synthesis is affected by auxin in mesophyll protoplas; (3) we have excised the corresponding gel slices and prepared antibodies against these proteins; (4) we have confirmed that they are the same proteins in calli and mesophyll and that they are present in roots but not in aerial organs

we have developed a method to produce specific antibodies against plant proteins by two‐dimensionary electrophoresis and have used these antibodies to study the expression patterns of three abundant proteins in tobacco.

the antibodies produced by the sera of the three rabbits injected with proteins extracted from callus are highly specific and recognize the same proteins in tobacco mesophyl protoplasts and in tobacco roots but not in aerial organs and in seeds, and that their synthesis is reduced by application of the phytohormone auxin.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the development of methods to produce high‐quality protein preparations for antibody production, and with the use of these antibodies to study the tissue specificity of protein accumulation in tobacco.
the development of an alternative method for the preparation of antibodies against proteins from a limited amount of tissue.
the production of specific antibodies against tobacco proteins, and the use of these antibodies to study the expression of these proteins during plant development.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the protein is a component of the plasma membrane of the root cells, and that it is not a protein that has been detected in the plasma membrane of tobacco mesophyll cells.
the use of 2D‐electrophoresis is a very powerful method for the production of antibodies against proteins whose synthesis has been reduced in plant cells by a specific treatment.
the three proteins are root‐specific and their synthesis in roots is reduced by auxins.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the preparation of protein extracts by phenol extraction and the separation of proteins by 2‐D electrophoresis allow the preparation of highly specific antibodies.
two‐dimensional gels are a powerful tool for protein preparation for antibody production.
we have prepared a high‐quality extract of proteins, separated them by non‐equilibrium two‐dimensional gel electrophoresis, and prepared antibodies for proteins of interest.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the use of two‐dimensional non‐equilibrium gels for the preparation of proteins for antibody synthesis is a rapid and efficient method.

the preparation of high quality protein extracts, followed by separation in non‐equilibrium gels and immunological characterization of the separated proteins is a powerful method for producing antibodies against proteins of interest.

the combination of the two‐dimensional separation techniques and phenol extraction allows the preparation of a large number of proteins from callus, and that the antibodies obtained can be used to detect the corresponding proteins in other organs and species.
